the brain network underlying cognitive dysfunction in Parkinson disease is different from the network underlying cognitive impairment in Alzheimer disease.
cognitive impairment in Parkinson’s disease (PD) is associated with a distinct brain network from that seen in Alzheimer disease (AD).
the cognitive impairment of PD is associated with the expression of a distinct network from that associated with cognitive impairment in AD.

the neural basis of cognitive impairment in Parkinson and Alzheimer disease.
the neurobiology of Parkinson disease and Alzheimer disease, two of the most common neurodegenerative diseases in older adults.
the neural basis of cognitive dysfunction in PD and AD.

cognitive dysfunction in Parkinson disease (and in Alzheimer disease) derives from the specific pathology of the disease itself, and not from a general pathology of aging or dementia.
cognitive dysfunction in PD is not associated with the same network pathology as seen in AD.

the network pathology underlying PD-related cognitive decline is distinct from that underlying AD-related cognitive decline, and the former is associated with a pattern of metabolic reduction in the basal ganglia and thalamus, whereas the latter is associated with a topographic pattern of reduction in the hippocampus and parietal-temporal cortex.
